title: Introduce Cost Automata blueprints and prefill tooling
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: provide a compact, auditable DSL and runtime templates for tenant-level prefill / batching defaults that encode unit-economics policies (budget caps, warmstart lanes, cache affordances, quantization tiers). This PR delivers a lightweight 'Cost Automata' blueprint format, a prefill CLI for dry-run simulations, runtime adapters to translate blueprints into existing prefill policies, and runbook docs. Design notes: Cost Automata are expressed as YAML state machines with explicit cost transitions and action hooks (e.g., increase_prefill, downgrade_quant_profile, fallback_route). The runtime adapter implements a safe two-step rollout: dry-run simulation -> telemetry validation -> soft-apply. Backwards compatibility: blueprint translator emits legacy-prefill policy objects to avoid breaking existing orchestration. Checklist: [x] DSL and schema v1 implemented, [x] CLI simulator (dry-run) added, [x] runtime adapter + translator implemented, [x] unit and integration tests, [x] runbook and examples, [x] e2e smoke validated on staging. Rollout plan: staged rollout to 10 tenants for 48h with telemetry gating, then gradual ramp. Related: builds on prefilling/sampler work and follows ENG-1984 decision tree. Quick links: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1984/cost-automata-design, runbook draft in docs/runbooks/prefill-blueprints.md. Migration: ops teams can run `prefill-cli simulate --blueprint examples/low_budget.yaml --dry-run` to validate. Implementation notes: prioritized safety (no automatic tenant-wide apply without opt-in), telemetry emits CostAutomataDecision events for audit and retrospective analysis.
